Linguistic competence (measurable): Place the 5 frequency adverbs correctly relative to the verb in ≥5 sentences; order them on a frequency scale.

Topic: Commerces — shopping, and the market exchange
SIO Description: Identify food shops (boulangerie, épicerie, boucherie, marché, supermarché); say where one shops; ask Combien ça coûte ? / Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît. Play both sides of a market exchange and know who says what: Je voudrais 2 kilos de pommes de terre. / Et avec ceci ? / Ça fait combien ? / C'est tout, merci ! / Ça fait 5,89 €.
Front side:
~10 shop cards — icon + English (e.g. 🥖 bakery / 🥩 butcher / 🐟 fishmonger)
plus ~8 exchange cards — English line + who says it
Back side (flipped):
French shop name + what it sells, or the French line
(e.g. une boulangerie — du pain, des croissants
🍎 Je voudrais deux kilos de pommes. — le client
➕ Et avec ceci ? — le marchand)
Overview columns: 1: Icon | 2: French | 3: English | 4: Products sold, or le marchand / le client | 5: Notes
Letris / Notes: 2 baskets: un / une for the shops; then order the exchange from Bonjour, vous désirez ? to Voici votre monnaie.
Can-Do (A1): I can shop for food, ask the price, ask for what I want politely, and handle a simple market exchange on either side of the stall.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Match ≥5 shops to what they sell; say where I shop; ask Combien ça coûte ? / Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît; assign each line of a market dialogue to le marchand or le client, put the exchange in order, and produce Je voudrais…, Ça fait combien ?, Et avec ceci ?

SIO Description: Understand and produce the numbers 70–99 — the soixante-dix and quatre-vingt system needed to handle real market prices: Ça fait quatre-vingt-cinq euros.
Front side:
~10 cards — the numeral (e.g. 70 / 85 / 91 / 99)
plus market price tags (e.g. 🏷️ 5,89 €)
Back side (flipped):
French number written out
(e.g. soixante-dix / quatre-vingt-cinq / quatre-vingt-onze / quatre-vingt-dix-neuf)
Overview columns: 1: Numeral | 2: French | 3: Built from: 60+10 / 4×20 / 4×20+10 | 4: Ça fait ___ euros. | 5: Notes
Letris / Notes: 3 baskets: soixante-dix… (60+10) / quatre-vingt… (4×20) / quatre-vingt-dix… (4×20+10)
Can-Do (A1): I can say and understand the numbers from 70 to 99, including in prices.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Count 70–99 following the soixante-dix / quatre-vingts patterns, and use them in market prices (Ça fait … euros).

SIO Description: Use ce/cet/cette/ces; apply correct form by gender and number (ce pain, cet ananas, cette tarte, ces légumes)
Front side:
~8 cards — noun + English with gender/number label
(e.g. 'this bread (m)' / 'this pineapple (m+vowel)' / 'these vegetables (pl)')
Back side (flipped):
French demonstrative + noun
(e.g. ce pain / cet ananas / cette tarte / ces légumes)
Overview columns: 1: French phrase | 2: English | 3: Gender/number | 4: Form (ce/cet/cette/ces) | 5: Notes
Letris / Notes: 4 baskets: ce / cet / cette / ces
Can-Do (A1): I can point out specific items (this/these) when shopping or ordering.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Select ce/cet/cette/ces correctly by gender/number for ≥8 nouns (≥80%).

SIO Description: Talk about plans with the futur proche: aller + infinitive across all persons (Je vais manger. / Nous allons visiter le marché.); say what you are going to do today, this weekend, after class
Front side:
~8 cards — English cue with the person
(e.g. 'I'm going to do sport' / 'we're going to visit the market')
Back side (flipped):
French futur proche — aller conjugated + infinitive
(e.g. Je vais faire du sport. / Nous allons visiter le marché. / Ils vont réserver pour huit heures.)
Overview columns: 1: French sentence | 2: English | 3: Person | 4: Form of aller | 5: Infinitive
Letris / Notes: 6 baskets by person: je vais / tu vas / il-elle va / nous allons / vous allez / ils-elles vont
Can-Do (A1): I can say what I am going to do.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Produce ≥5 futur-proche sentences with correctly conjugated aller + infinitive.

SIO Description: Give simple advice with tu dois + inf (personal obligation), il faut + inf (general necessity) and tu peux + inf (suggestion): Tu dois dormir plus. / Il faut manger des légumes. / Tu peux prendre le bus.
Front side:
~9 cards — English cue with the function
(e.g. 'suggestion: you can taste' / 'obligation: you must eat vegetables' / 'general rule: one must drink water')
Back side (flipped):
French advice with the matching structure
(e.g. Tu peux goûter. / Tu dois manger des légumes. / Il faut boire de l'eau.)
Overview columns: 1: French phrase | 2: English | 3: Structure: pouvoir / devoir / falloir | 4: Function: suggestion / personal obligation / general necessity | 5: Notes
Letris / Notes: 3 baskets: pouvoir (tu peux) / devoir (tu dois) / falloir (il faut)
Can-Do (A1): I can give simple advice about food, health and daily life.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Give ≥5 pieces of advice using devoir/falloir/pouvoir + infinitive with correct forms.

SIO Description: Give a simple restaurant review with positive and negative points (C'est délicieux ! / Le service est lent. / C'est trop cher mais c'est bon. / Je recommande / Je ne recommande pas.)
Front side:
~8 cards — evaluation cue
(e.g. '👍 delicious food' / '👎 slow service' / '💰 too expensive')
Back side (flipped):
French evaluation phrase
(e.g. C'est délicieux ! / Le service est lent.
/ C'est trop cher mais c'est bon.
/ Je recommande ce restaurant !)
Overview columns: 1: French phrase | 2: English | 3: + or − | 4: Notes
Letris / Notes: 2 baskets: positif / négatif
Can-Do (A1): I can give a simple opinion about a restaurant, mentioning good and bad points.
Linguistic competence (measurable): State ≥1 positive point, ≥1 negative point, and a clear recommendation (Je recommande / Je ne recommande pas).

SIO Description: Role-play a complete restaurant interaction: greet the waiter, read the menu, order (entrée/plat/boisson/dessert), interact during the meal, ask for the bill, pay and say goodbye
Letris / Notes: ⛔ Production/spoken task — no flashcard
Can-Do (A1): I can get by in a simple restaurant visit from arrival to paying, using set phrases, as long as staff are patient.
Linguistic competence (measurable): Complete all 6 steps: greet, read the menu, order (entrée/plat/boisson/dessert), interact, ask for the bill, pay and say goodbye.
